problem: Let $u=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1 \\ -3 \\ 3\end{aligned}],v=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -2 \\ 2 \\ -4\end{aligned}]$ and $w=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$ be vectors such that $u\,⊥\,w.$ Find $(w+v)\cdot (2u+3w).$
worked_solution:
Since $u$ and $w$ are orthogonal vectors, we have that $u\cdot w=0.$ Therefore, using linearity of the dot product to expand the parentheses, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(w+v)\cdot (2u+3w) & =2(w\cdot u)+2(v\cdot u)+3(w\cdot w)+3(v\cdot w) \\  & =0+2(v\cdot u)+3(w\cdot w)+3(v\cdot w) \\  & =2(v\cdot u)+3(w\cdot w)+3(v\cdot w) \\  & =2(-4\cdot 5+(-2)\cdot 1+2\cdot (-3)+(-4)\cdot 3) \\  & +3(1\cdot 1+(-5)\cdot (-5)+2\cdot 2+2\cdot 2) \\  & +3(-4\cdot 1+(-2)\cdot (-5)+2\cdot 2+(-4)\cdot 2) \\  & =2(-40)+3(34)+3(2) \\  & =-80+102+6 \\  & =28.\end{aligned}
$$
